_comment: Player contract: bump whenever pack.ts starts emitting something an older player/game.js cannot read. The player build stamps this into public/player/build.json; publishClient refuses to publish when the two disagree, and the player refuses to boot a game.bin from a newer packer. v1 = every bundle built before the guard existed (no build.json at all) -- notably the 2026-07-22 bundle that predates terrain heightChunk/splatChunk and animation-field playback. v3 adds tilemap cell chunks: a v2 player ignores `chunk` on a tile chunk and would render an empty map with nothing logged, which is exactly the silent failure this number exists to prevent. v4 moves UI out of `scenes[].ui` and into UI nodes in the scene tree: a v3 player has no UI node classes, so parseNodeJson falls through to Node.parse and the game renders no HUD at all, silently -- again exactly what this number exists to catch. v5 moves SHARED animation clips out of the serialized nodes and into a game-level `animations` array (with `modelAnimations` saying which model plays which), retargeted onto each character at load: a v4 player never runs that step, so every character that uses a shared clip stands in its bind pose with nothing logged. v6 moves a skinned model's per-vertex bone data (`jointIndices`/`jointWeights`) out of the manifest JSON and into blob chunks, because Model.serialize now writes those as typed arrays and a typed array stringifies as {"0":..} rather than an array: a v5 player finds neither the chunk it does not know about nor a readable array, so every skinned character loads with no bone weights and collapses to the origin -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v7 adds NavMeshNode: a v6 player has no such class, so parseNodeJson falls through to Node.parse, scene.navMeshes comes back empty, and every controller on a `path` or `patrol` goal falls back to walking in a straight line into the geometry it was supposed to route around -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v8 adds DecalNode: a v7 player has no such class, so parseNodeJson falls through to Node.parse, each decal loads as a plain Node with its `decal` payload dropped, and every scorch mark, painted road line and area-of-effect ring is missing from the published game -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v9 replaces the terrain's 4-layer normalized splat with a layer STACK: a base landscape material plus ordered paint layers, each with a mask channel in a `masksChunk`, and slot rules evaluated in the shader. A v8 player knows `splatChunk` and four `layers`, finds neither, and draws every landscape in its base colour with no painted roads, no rules and no foliage rules bound to a layer -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v10 adds controller LAYERS, action SLOTS, pose states, clip-owned events and skeleton SOCKETS (`stateMachine.layers/slots`, `state.pose`, `animation.events`, `skin.sockets`, node `socketAttachment`): a v9 player ignores all of them, so an upper-body layer never plays, a held weapon stays where it was placed instead of following the hand, and footstep events on clips never fire -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v11 adds ParticleSystemNode and ForceFieldNode: a v10 player has no such classes, so parseNodeJson falls through to Node.parse, each loads as a plain Node with its `particleSystem` / `forceField` payload dropped, and every fire, spark, smoke plume and wind zone is missing from the published game -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v12 adds WaterVolumeNode: a v11 player has no such class, so parseNodeJson falls through to Node.parse, the `waterVolume` payload is dropped, and nothing floats -- crates and logs sink through the pond and the surface never ripples -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v13 adds anatomical ragdoll profiles (skin.ragdollProfile, ragdollProfile.ts): a v12 player has no profile builder, so every death falls as the old generic per-bone ragdoll -- 1 kg spheres on the joints, knees bending both ways -- with nothing to say why. v14 gives every scene its own render settings (`scenes[].render`), applied as the player starts it: a v13 player ignores them, so a game that walks from a daylit valley into a dark dungeon shows the dungeon through the valley's exposure, shadows and post -- black, or blown out -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v15 adds ExposureVolumeNode: a v14 player has no such class, so parseNodeJson falls through to Node.parse, the `exposureVolume` payload is dropped, and a cave or interior authored with its own exposure is shown through the scene-wide exposure instead -- blown out or crushed -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v16 adds ClothNode: a v15 player has no such class, so parseNodeJson falls through to Node.parse, the `cloth` payload is dropped, and every cape, banner and flag is missing from the published game -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v17 adds trigger OPTIONS (`trigger.enabled/group/mask/detectTriggers/continuous`) and trigger-to-trigger overlaps: a v16 player ignores them, so every trigger loads enabled, in layer 1, detecting only moving bodies -- a hurtbox never sees a hitbox and a switched-off hitbox is live -- and a combat game deals no damage at all, silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v18 replaces OccluderNode with OcclusionVolumeNode (type `occlusionVolume`): a box whose CONTENTS are skipped while the box cannot be seen, where an `occluder` hid what was BEHIND it. A v17 player has no such class, so parseNodeJson falls through to Node.parse and the volume hides nothing -- silently slower, never wrong -- while a v17 player reading a legacy `occluder` would rasterize a volume fitted round a room as a solid wall and cull what you can see past it, which is what this number exists to catch. v19 adds VolumetricFogNode (type `volumetricFog`), moonlight in lux (`atmosphere.moonIlluminance`), physical sky units (`atmosphere.physicalUnits`), light flicker (`light.flicker`) and light-following sprites and particle systems (`followLight`, `fogGlow`): a v18 player has no fog class, so parseNodeJson falls through to Node.parse and every fog bank is missing, and it reads a lux moon as the default fraction of the sun -- a moon as bright as day -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v20 makes WeatherNode a bounded box volume (`weather.size/blendDistance/priority/enabled`), several of which may overlap, adds puddles, a snow material (`weather.snowMaterial`, `snowMaterialId`, `snowTiling/Slope/Breakup`) and shelter (`weather.shelter`), and draws wetness and snow on the landscape: a v19 player reads a bounded volume as scene-wide weather on the foliage alone, so a snowy hilltop box snows every plant in the game and leaves the ground bare -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v21 adds the AgX Punchy tone mapper (`render.toneMapper: 'agxPunchy'`) and makes the physical sky's march converge, calibrated to measured daylight: a v20 player has no such curve and falls back to plain AgX, so the clear sky turns steel-grey again, and it marches a physical sky in even steps to its atmosphere's top, so a thick atmosphere comes out up to 17 times too dark -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v22 turns cylindrical sprites to face the camera's POSITION about their own upright axis (they lay parallel to the screen, squashed and leaning at the corners of a wide view), shadows light-probe captures with a sun map of their own, keeps a deferred probe slot for the unbounded fallback probe and hands the other to the volume the camera is in, takes a normal map's lost mip detail into the roughness, fixes the split-sum Fresnel that made rough ground glossy at grazing angles, and floors a lit smoke sprite's local lights at its own thickness: a v21 player draws the same game with sprites lying flat to the screen, probes lit through their own hills and roofs, and a white orb in the smoke over every fire at night -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v23 applies a light probe's LIGHTING per pixel from every lighting probe in view, as spherical harmonics in the deferred pass's uniform block (and per draw for forward materials, per effect for lit particles and sprites), where it used to come from the two cubemap slots handed out by the camera's position; the slots now carry reflections alone: a v22 player lights a room from its probe only while the camera stands inside it, so a house looked into through its door is lit like the street and darkens with a jump on the threshold -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v24 applies probe REFLECTIONS per pixel from one octahedral reflection atlas (and box-projects them, `lightProbe.boxProjection`), bakes and relights probes in time-sliced jobs, and leaves lights with `light.bake` false out of probe captures: a v23 player reflects whatever probe box the camera stands in on every surface, ignores box projection and the bake flag, and captures every probe whole in one frame -- a hitch each time the sun moves -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch.
